Against IDH-wildtype, T2-FLAIR Mismatch Present with a high T2-FLAIR Mismatch Score is a recognized imaging marker of IDH-mutant astrocytoma, and Tumor Location / Region Proportions indicate a cortical temporal lesion that can fit IDH-mutant diffuse glioma; Enhancement Quality is only mild. Overall, the age, enhancement/necrosis, extensive edema, mass effect, and invasive ventricular/deep white matter features outweigh the T2-FLAIR mismatch signal, so the best estimate is IDH-wildtype.

overall_comment: Predictions are based only on structural MRI metadata without diffusion, perfusion, spectroscopy, or susceptibility/calcification assessment. The main uncertainty is the strong T2-FLAIR mismatch signal, which argues for an IDH-mutant astrocytic tumor, but the patient age and aggressive enhancing/necrotic, edematous, mass-effect and ventricular/deep white matter invasive features favor IDH-wildtype grade 4 disease. Tissue diagnosis with molecular testing remains required.

who_grade.reasoning: Independent WHO grade assessment: ET Volume (mL), Proportion Enhancing, Thickness of enhancing margin, NCR Volume (mL), and Proportion Necrosis indicate enhancing and necrotic tumor components, which favor high-grade disease and support grade 4 over grade 2 or 3. ED Volume (mL), Proportion of Oedema, Total tumor volume (mL), midline_shift_present, max_shift_mm, Deep WM invasion, and Ependymal (ventricular) Invasion further support aggressive biology with substantial mass effect and invasion. Against grade 4, Enhancement Quality is mild, Proportion Enhancing and Proportion Necrosis are relatively limited fractions of the whole tumor, T2-FLAIR Mismatch Present can be seen in lower-grade IDH-mutant astrocytoma, and Multifocal or Multicentric / Multiple satellites present do not show multifocal spread. Overall, the presence of enhancement plus necrosis with extensive edema, mass effect, and ventricular/deep white matter invasion most strongly supports CNS WHO grade 4.
